properties.description: A two-tiered waterfall tucked in Barangay San Antonio, Remedios T. Romualdez — cold, clear pools and a laid-back cottage area about 45 minutes from Butuan City.
properties.entrance_fee: Reasonable entrance fee (~₱30–50); cottage rental extra
properties.best_season: Dry season, Nov–May (fuller flow, easier footing on the stone steps)
properties.family_friendly: The steps down to the base pool are a little worn, so hold little hands on the way down; the pools themselves are calm enough for kids to wade and swim once you're there.

properties.description: A breezy hilltop park in Carmen, right on the boundary of Agusan del Norte and Misamis Oriental, with sweeping views toward the coast and Camiguin on a clear day.
properties.best_season: Year-round; clearest views in the dry season, Nov–May
properties.family_friendly: No swimming or strenuous trekking involved — just a scenic stop to stretch, take photos, and let kids run around; there's a videoke machine if your family likes to sing, and a police/military checkpoint nearby keeps the area safe.

properties.description: A hilltop eco-historical park overlooking the Masao River and Butuan Bay, believed by locals to be tied to one of the earliest Catholic masses held in Mindanao.
properties.best_season: Year-round; go in the morning for cooler, quieter walking weather
properties.family_friendly: Easy, flat strolling paths and open lawns make this a low-effort stop with older kids who can appreciate the history; note that restroom facilities have been reported as poorly maintained, so plan accordingly.

properties.description: Siargao's famous tidal rock pools in Pilar — clear, emerald pools that only appear at low tide, ringed by dramatic rock formations.
properties.best_season: Dry season, Mar–May, and only around low tide — check the local tide schedule before you go
properties.family_friendly: The rocks get sharp and slippery, so water shoes are a must for kids; a roped-off shallow area makes it safer for younger swimmers, but keep an eye on tide times since the pools disappear at high tide.

properties.description: A four-tiered waterfall in an ecological park near Prosperidad, widely considered the most popular falls in Agusan del Sur — each tier has its own character, with Falls 3 the biggest.
properties.best_season: Dry season, Nov–May (still flows year-round, but paths are easier when dry)
properties.family_friendly: There are a lot of stairs between tiers, so it suits families who can handle a bit of a hike; life jackets are available to rent for less confident swimmers, and cottages are available for a rest afterward.

properties.description: A wide, soft white-sand beach in Cagwait facing the sunrise, with local stores and eateries just steps from the shore.
properties.entrance_fee: Free; cottage rental fees may apply
properties.best_season: Dry season, Mar–May for the calmest water
properties.family_friendly: The wide, gently sloping sand is easy for young kids to play on, and food stalls nearby mean you won't have to pack a full picnic; waves can pick up at times, so keep smaller swimmers close to shore.

properties.description: Dramatic, wave-carved limestone cliffs off Basilisa, reachable by a short boat ride — one of Dinagat's most photographed natural landmarks.
properties.entrance_fee: Free (boat transport costs extra, shared across your group)
properties.best_season: Dry season, Mar–May, when seas are calmest for the boat crossing
properties.family_friendly: Swimming isn't allowed here due to strong currents, so treat it as a scenic photo stop rather than a swim spot — genuinely striking for kids who like dramatic scenery, but keep them back from the water's edge.

properties.description: The Roman Catholic cathedral at the heart of Tandag City, seat of the Diocese of Tandag and a long-standing landmark of Surigao del Sur's Spanish-era religious heritage.
properties.best_season: Year-round; check ahead if you'd like to time a visit around Mass
properties.family_friendly: A quick, easy stop right in the city center — good for a short heritage break between longer drives; dress modestly and keep noise down if a service is in progress.
